scope: Bounded revision 4 design and abstract Lean propositions; approval does not assert implementation or quality gate completion.
findings: The admitted member binds its own run, witness, target and polarity through the inherited SAT and validated admission predicate; ready requires N distinct members per polarity for 3 through 5.
The declared queries preserve facts in both polarities and finite shared samples are not equivalence evidence. Exact context and canonical full-instance comparisons guard overlap.
The pack4 lookup propositions bind each of four ordered 768-entry blocks to a 3072-entry abstract embedding. The numeric score theorem covers only the default nonnegative fixed-point weights.

Current complete snapshots are required in the abstract commit model and revoked entries are invisible; the concrete transaction, outbox and independent revocation journal remain implementation obligations.
The revision distinguishes checked egraph representatives from a complete normal form, requires evidence-bound pool identity and preserves authorized filtering and train lineage on revocation.
limitations: The model assumes exact identity tokens and truthful validation flags; SAT4J, parser, evaluator, instance isomorphism, hashing and encoding correspondence are trusted and require adversarial implementation tests.

The Lean type Int-valued function represents indexing, not float normalization, E5 embeddings or learned adapter behavior. Fixed-point score bounds do not establish floating-point numerical correctness or tuned-weight correctness.
Abstract commit and visibility predicates do not prove PostgreSQL atomicity, crash recovery, authorization, deletion, model lineage revocation or Java/Python refinement.

Two frozen clean builds and independent review resolution are required before production changes; this review does not claim those checks passed. Dataset rights, retrieval quality and all original gates require separate evidence.
